newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hannover Re sees further profit rise in 97.
newsitem.headline: Hannover Re sees further profit rise in 97.

text.p: German reinsurance group Hannover Rueckversicherungs AG said on Thursday it expected another double digit percentage rise in profits this year after reporting a 36 percent rise in earnings for 1996.
Management board chairman Wilhelm Zeller told a news conference that the group, known as Hannover Re, had seen a favourable claims development in the first months of the year.
"We have made a commitment to shareholders to increase our earnings and dividend at a double-digit rate annually," Zeller said.

This year's underwriting profit would no longer be hit by excessive costs, Zeller said. However earnings from capital investments would not be as exceptionally high as they were in 1996, when currency effects boosted the figure sharply.
Preliminary results for 1996 showed Hannover Re's pre-tax profit rose 36 percent to 158 million marks while premiums rose seven percent to 6.4 billion.
Premiums would rise some three percent, in line with the market trend, in 1997, Zeller predicted.
